title: Cross-host CI defect burn-down
description: Objective: make the EXISTING cross-host workflow (ubuntu+macos gate jobs, .github/workflows/cross-host.yml) green by fixing a bounded, named defect set - NOT by building new portability features. Context: the gate has failed 10 consecutive push runs, all grading commit 52584ea; local HEAD is 5-6 commits ahead and CI has never seen it, so FIRST re-measure after the pending push of moe/work-2026-08-08 lands. An independent review (2026-08-18) names 5 defect classes claimed to cover the ~7 shared failures - treat each as a CLAIM to re-measure at current HEAD before fixing, per the staleness rail: (1) daemon index.ts held-out leak (claimed to fix 2 suites); (2) claude runtime discovery on linux/macos; (3) windows-boundary broker behavior on non-Windows hosts; (4) macOS phase0 TMPDIR symlink class (see memory: macos-tmpdir-symlink-reads-as-path-escape); (5) JetBrains port-arm code (CI-green fix only - do NOT build adapter features; the JetBrains adapter itself is parked to v0.2). Scope guard: this task fixes deterministic test/code defects visible in the existing gate legs; any fix that grows into a feature reports blocked instead. SEQUENCING: run after the 5 local commits are pushed and one fresh CI run grades current HEAD - its failure list is the authoritative work list, not the review's. Verification: gate-leg commands green locally where reproducible (pnpm typecheck && pnpm test with count lines) plus a green ubuntu+macos gate run URL on the final commit.
definitionOfDone: A fresh CI run on current HEAD is captured FIRST and its failing-test list recorded in a task comment as the authoritative baseline (the review's 5-defect list re-measured against it, matches and mismatches disclosed).
Every deterministic failure in the baseline is fixed in its owning package or quarantined with a filed follow-up task id; no test deleted or excluded to go green.
The ubuntu and macos gate jobs are green on the task's final pushed commit, evidenced by the run URL.
pnpm typecheck and pnpm test exit 0 locally with nonzero Test Files count lines; only explicit owned paths committed, each fix disclosed per package.
taskRails: Fix defects, not features: no new adapter/portability surface; a fix growing beyond a defect reports blocked.
Re-measure before fixing: the review's defect list is a claim, the fresh CI run is the baseline.
Assert the reason code on every refusal-path test touched; per-file 250/400 caps hold.

CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_DUPLICATE at RUNTIME"; (4) packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-spec.test.ts "keeps the held-out models out of every production module"; (5) packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.test.ts "publishes exactly the anchor surface a restore controller composes"; (6) tests/integration/portability/transport-host-matrix.test.ts "answers each JetBrains port arm with an exact IDE-layer code". Ubuntu: 6 files / 7 tests of 7407; macOS: 7 files / 13 tests. Review-claim reconciliation: claims 1-5 ALL confirmed; recovery-anchor is a SIXTH class the review missed. NOW: push the pending local commits EXPLICITLY (`git push origin moe/work-2026-08-08` — the task's own sequencing step; never force, never a different ref), await the push-triggered cross-host run on the pushed HEAD (`gh run list --workflow=cross-host.yml --limit 1`, then `gh run view <id> --log-failed`), record ITS failing list verbatim, and post the baseline + reconciliation as a TASK COMMENT via moe.add_comment. implementationPlan.description: CLASS A — claude runtime discovery/request (3 tests, one seam, both hosts). Diagnose from the fresh run's assertion text (`gh run view <id> --log-failed`, the failing expect lines are in the log) plus local code reading of packages/runner/src/providers/claude/claude-runtime-discovery.ts and claude-runtime-request.ts: these tests PASS on win32 and fail on linux+macos, so the defect is platform-conditional (candidate: discovery roots/executable names/PATHEXT semantics that only exist on win32, or a fixture path that hard-codes a Windows shape). Fix the DEFECT in the owning package — either the production discovery honestly refusing/answering per-platform with its existing codes, or the test building per-platform fixtures — NEVER a skip/exclusion, NEVER a new portability feature (task rail 1: a fix growing into a feature reports blocked). Every refusal assertion touched keeps its exact code+layer (CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_DUPLICATE at RUNTIME stays pinned literally). Local leg: `pnpm --filter @moe/runner test` green with count line on Windows; the linux/macos proof arrives via the step-6 push run.
implementationPlan.note:
CLASS A fixed, commit 5de0c42 (explicit pathspec, 2 files).

Root cause, measured not guessed -- both are FIXTURE defects, production untouched:
1. claude-runtime-discovery.test.ts:152 called standInDirectory() unconditionally for the duplicate case; standInDirectory does copyFileSync("C:\\Windows\\System32\\where.exe", ...) so off Windows the fixture died with ENOENT before discoverInstalledClaudeRuntime() could answer. Every OTHER host-configuring case in the same file already uses `ON_WINDOWS ? standInDirectory(x) : temporaryDirectory(x)` (lines 161, 173) -- the duplicate case just missed it. The refusal assertion is untouched: CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PATH_DUPLICATE at RUNTIME on win32, CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED at RUNTIME off it, both already pinned literally in the file.
2. claude-runtime-request.test.ts: the two host-arm cases used `nativeJoin` on the off-Windows literal root "C:\\moe-absent-root", producing "C:\\moe-absent-root/pins". claude-runtime-source.ts:79 LOCAL_ABSOLUTE rejects mixed separators -> "a runtime pin request path is not an absolute local-drive Windows path" from the SHAPE guard, so the host-observation arm under test was never reached. Now built with win32.join, which IS nativeJoin on win32 (zero change there) and yields a true Windows shape elsewhere.
Reason-code rail: the UNKNOWN case previously accepted the whole CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PIN_ERROR_CODES roster. Off Windows prepareClaudeRuntimePin's own platform guard (claude-runtime-pin.ts:181) answers BEFORE any observation, so roster-containment would have let the case read as "the observation refused" on a host where it never ran. Now: roster containment on win32, exact CLAUDE_RUNTIME_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED off it. The arm-sweep case's off-Windows collapse onto one arm is disclosed in a comment rather than hidden; its oracle is still production's own answer for the same input.

Local proof (win32): pnpm exec vitest run <both files> -> exit 0, Test Files 2 passed (2), Tests 53 passed (53). Linux/macOS proof arrives with the step-6 push run.

implementationPlan.description: CLASS B — windows-boundary broker on non-Windows hosts (1 test, both hosts). The failing test's own comment (log line 522) says "On this host the broker IS built. A missing binary must FAIL ra[ther than skip]" — read packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-boundary.test.ts's broker-resolution block and the production resolver it tests: on ubuntu/macos the pinned-toolchain release broker binary legitimately does not exist, so either the TEST's host-guard is wrong (it should assert the resolver's own non-Windows refusal arm with its exact code, not expect a built binary) or the resolver misreports the host. Fix whichever is the defect, preserving the fail-closed stance: a missing binary ON WINDOWS must still FAIL. Assert the non-Windows arm's exact reason code (read the resolver's vocabulary; never bare-null assert). No new broker build steps in CI — that would be a feature (report blocked if the only fix is building the broker on linux/macos).
implementationPlan.note:
CLASS B fixed, commit e98c5f3 (1 file, explicit pathspec). Test defect, resolver untouched.

Diagnosis: packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-broker-path.ts resolveBrokerBinary() is platform-blind by design -- it locates the workspace root by pnpm-workspace.yaml and stats dist/windows-job-native/release/moe-windows-job-broker.exe, returning the absolute path or unresolved("the release broker binary has not been built"). That binary is a WINDOWS executable produced by a Windows-targeted cargo build into a git-ignored dist/ (.gitignore:4, no prebuilt binary vendored), so on ubuntu/macos it is absent BY CONSTRUCTION and the resolver correctly answers its typed UNKNOWN. The defect was the test asserting typeof resolved === "string" on every host. The resolver did NOT misreport the host -- it is honest; the case's premise ("On this host the broker IS built") was Windows-only prose.

Fix per the step's own instruction: off-Windows the case asserts the resolver's exact vocabulary -- code PROCESS_BOUNDARY_BROKER_UNRESOLVED, layer WINDOWS_PROCESS_RESOLUTION, routed through the file's existing unknownOf() which itself throws unless truthClass is UNKNOWN. Not a skip: the branch asserts, it does not return early unasserted. On win32 the fail-closed stance is byte-identical to before -- a missing binary still reddens.

No CI broker build was added (that would be the feature this task's rail forbids).

Local proof (win32, broker present at dist/windows-job-native/release/moe-windows-job-broker.exe): pnpm exec vitest run packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-boundary.test.ts -> exit 0, Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 86 passed (86). The off-Windows branch is exercised by the step-6 push run.

implementationPlan.description: CLASS C — testkit pair. (C1) foundation-spec.test.ts "keeps the held-out models out of every production module" (both hosts): this is a SCAN test — read its scan roots and matcher, then find which production module now references a held-out model name (the review claims the daemon index.ts leak; verify by running the same scan logic locally — the test is platform-independent in intent, so ALSO check why it passes on win32 but fails on linux/macos: a path-separator or case-sensitivity artifact in the scan itself is the likelier defect; a scan that silently narrows on win32 is exactly the sweep-goes-vacuous class from the global rails). Fix the leak in its owning module OR the scan's platform blindness — both are defects; adding a Windows-blind exclusion is not. (C2) phase0-node-capture-port.test.ts, 6 tests, MACOS-ONLY: the known TMPDIR class — /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp on macOS, so realpath-vs-lexical comparisons read as path escapes / wrong-repo redirects (memory macos-tmpdir-symlink-reads-as-path-escape). Fix in the capture port or the test fixtures by canonicalizing consistently (realpathSync on BOTH operands at the comparison boundary, or building fixtures under an already-canonical root) — preserving every refusal's exact code; the oversize/atomic-store failures in the same file likely share the fixture root cause, so re-diagnose them AFTER the symlink fix rather than patching six tests independently.
implementationPlan.note:
CLASS C. C1 = NO WORK NEEDED (re-measured closed); C2 fixed, commit 8dfda88 (1 file).

C1 (foundation-spec "keeps the held-out models out of every production module"): re-measured GREEN in the step-1 baseline run 32232031394 on both hosts. It was closed by peer commit 1ccde5f, already in local HEAD when this task started. The step's own hypothesis is the one that held: the defect was in the SCAN, not a leak. The old matcher spelled `foundation[\\/]` bare, which false-positived on apps/daemon/src/foundation/ -- the daemon's OWN production surface, imported at apps/daemon/src/index.ts:232 -- so the review's "daemon index.ts held-out leak" was the sweep mis-reading a legitimate intra-daemon import. The matcher now reads /(?:from|import|require)\s*\(?\s*["'][^"']*testkit[\\/][^"']*foundation[^"']*["']/u, anchored on the testkit package where the held-out models actually live. Its char class is [\\/], so it is separator-agnostic; the sweep still pins its floor with expect(files.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(100), so it cannot go vacuous. No Windows-blind exclusion exists or was added. Verified locally: 74 tests green across foundation-spec + recovery-anchor.

C2 (phase0-node-capture-port, 6 macOS-only tests): ONE fixture root cause, as the step predicted. temporaryDirectory() built its root with mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), ...)) and never canonicalised it. On macOS $TMPDIR is under /var/folders and /var symlinks to /private/var, so the root has a symlinked ANCESTOR. phase0-node-paths.ts:106 requireStableRoot lstats the root (must not itself be a symlink) AND requires realpath(root) === root -- arm two is what macOS trips. Both failing arms are the guard's real subject (a redirected root), so relaxing it would have made it vacuous: samePath(realpath(x), realpath(x)) can never refuse. Fixed in the fixture instead -- realpath once at creation, every derived path inherits it. Production untouched, every refusal code unchanged. This also explains the two cases that asserted a DIFFERENT code (PHASE0_NODE_GIT_TOP_LEVEL_MISMATCH, PHASE0_NODE_FILE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) and got PATH_ESCAPE instead: an earlier guard was answering, which is the refusal-test-answered-by-earlier-guard class. Post-fix each reaches its own subject -- proven off-Windows by the step-6 run; nothing was patched per-test.

Local proof (win32): node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run packages/testkit/src/phase0-node-capture-port.test.ts -> exit 0, Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 10 passed (10).
Environment note for the next agent: `pnpm exec vitest` began failing mid-session with pnpm's deps-status check demanding `pnpm install --production` (a peer has apps/daemon/package.json modified in the shared worktree). Invoking `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs` directly bypasses that check and leaves node_modules alone; do NOT set CI=true to silence it, that authorises a modules purge.

CLASS D. D1 = NO WORK NEEDED (re-measured closed); D2 fixed, commit 015bdc4 (1 file).

D1 (recovery-anchor "publishes exactly the anchor surface a restore controller composes"): re-measured GREEN on both hosts in baseline run 32232031394. Closed by peer commit ad6c42c, already in local HEAD at task start. Root cause was neither enumeration order nor path separators: RECOVERY_ANCHOR_FAULT_POINTS sat in the test's WITHHELD roster while the fault suite tests/fault/disaster-restore/anchor-boundary-crash.fault.ts sweeps every fault point OFF the root barrel, so the producer had to publish it. The row moved WITHHELD -> PUBLISHED (recovery-anchor.test.ts:663-665, with the reason recorded inline) and packages/store/src/index.ts:95 exports it. The exact-equality stance is intact -- PUBLISHED is checked defined and WITHHELD checked undefined; nothing was loosened to containment. Verified locally green.

D2 (transport-host-matrix "answers each JetBrains port arm with an exact IDE-layer code"): fixture defect in the child probe script, no adapter code touched (JetBrains stays parked to v0.2). daemonCommand pointed at node_modules/.bin/moe-daemon(.CMD). On win32 node refuses to spawn a .CMD without a shell, so launchDetached (adapters/jetbrains/src/host/jetbrains-host-ports.ts:115) resolved !ok -> evidence REFUSED -> decideDaemonStart returns DAEMON_START_REFUSED at DAEMON_START_PORT. That arm was green BY ACCIDENT of node's .cmd guard. On linux/macos the shim exists and launches, the deliberately-closed deadPort never confirms listening, the bounded confirm loop times out, evidence is LAUNCHED_UNCONFIRMED and adapters/ide-contract/src/index.ts:200 answers DAEMON_START_UNVERIFIED -- correct production behaviour for what the fixture actually did. It also left a detached daemon on those runners. daemonCommand now names a path inside the probe's temp dir that is never created, so spawn fails ENOENT on every host and the arm refuses for ONE stated reason. Only the dead host ever launches: the live/reconnect/post-uninstall arms reconnect to the child's own listener and the mismatch/assets arms refuse earlier, so no other case is affected. The expectation roster is unchanged -- DAEMON_START_REFUSED is still pinned at runtime against IDE_ADAPTER_REASON_CODES read out of @moe/ide-adapter-contract in the child, so a production rename still reddens.

Local proof (win32): node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/integration/portability/transport-host-matrix.test.ts -> exit 0, Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 14 passed (14). That run executes the child probe script end to end, which is also the syntax check this file gets (integration sources are typechecked by nothing).
